data.title: Zhu Rongji, trailblazing ex-premier who transformed China's economy
data.description: BEIJING - Zhu Rongji, China's former premier who died on Wednesday aged 97, championed free-market policies and delivered far-reaching economic reforms during his five years at the helm.

data.title: Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji dies aged 97
data.description: BEIJING - Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji, whose market reforms helped drive the country's extraordinary economic rise, died Wednesday at the age of 97.

data.title: WHO says Trump vaccine shake-up goes against evidence
data.description: GENEVA - The World Health Organization warned Wednesday that Donald Trump's bid to overhaul child vaccination in the United States goes against "decades of evidence".

data.title: Mideast war impact on travel bookings fading, TUI says
data.description: FRANKFURT (GERMANY) - German travel giant TUI said Wednesday that bookings were returning to normal levels despite the ongoing Mideast war, as it presented its latest financial results.

data.title: Japan brushes off Australian PM's melon drama
data.description: TOKYO - Tokyo has played down comments by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese about melons gifted to him by his Japanese counterpart that have triggered a row Down Under, stressing the leaders' good relationship.

data.title: Meta meets its own 'tobacco' moment in court
data.description: OAKLAND (UNITED STATES) - With billions of users around the world, Meta has prepared to defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media's big tobacco moment.

data.title: Australian delivery drivers win 'world-leading' pay rise
data.description: SYDNEY - Hundreds of thousands of gig workers in Australia have been granted a huge pay rise from next week under a decision by the country's workplace relations tribunal lauded as "world-leading".

data.title: Art or medicine? Japan's cosmetic tattoo artists in limbo
data.description: GINOWAN (JAPAN) - Tattoo artist Remy painstakingly injects tiny dots of pigment into customer Koki Hatanaka's bald scalp to mimic hair follicles, performing a grey-zone cosmetic procedure that has increasingly been in the crosshairs of Japanese health authorities.

data.title: Parched and desperate for rain, Kazakhstan turns to cloud-seeding
data.description: TURKESTAN (KAZAKHSTAN) - There were only arid steppes in sight when a small plane took off from an airport in southern Kazakhstan, embarking on a delicate mission: bringing rain for the scorched earth below.

data.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year's mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

data.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
data.description: MATARAM (INDONESIA) - A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

data.title: 2.4 million girls banned from Afghan schools since Taliban return: UNESCO
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Around 2.4 million girls in Afghanistan have been denied access to secondary education since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, the United Nations said Tuesday, urging an end to such "discrimination".

data.title: Cuba celebrates Castro's 100th as his revolution faces its toughest test
data.description: HAVANA - As Cuba marks 100 years since Fidel Castro's birth, Cubans are questioning the promises of the socialist revolution he led for nearly half a century, and asking whether his successors are up to the job.

data.title: Barred from elections, Russia's anti-war party vows to fight on
data.description: MOSCOW - When 18-year-old Karina learnt the party she supported ahead of her first parliamentary election in Russia was barred from contesting, she was shocked -- but also surprised by what happened next.

data.title: What to know about the total solar eclipse
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Day will briefly turn into night across a swathe of northern Spain on Wednesday, when the Moon will completely cover the Sun during a rare total solar eclipse.

data.title: Total solar eclipse to spellbind Europe
data.description: BURGOS (SPAIN) - Millions of Europeans will contemplate the sky in awe on Wednesday as a rare total solar eclipse crosses part of the continent and plunges a swathe of Spain into eerie daytime darkness.

data.title: Trump's secret plane swap triggers questions and confusion
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - A secret operation that reportedly smuggled Donald Trump off Air Force One in a catering truck before the plane departed carrying journalists and staff at apparent risk of an Iranian strike has raised questions over US security practices.

data.title: Colombia scrambles to find survivors as quake kills 240
data.description: PEREIRA (COLOMBIA) - Colombian volunteers on Tuesday dredged through rubble, searching for survivors from an earthquake that killed at least 240 people and leveled more than a hundred homes and office buildings.

data.title: UN says 2 staff arrested by Afghan intelligence agency
data.description: KABUL - Two staff members of the United Nations mission in Afghanistan have been arrested by the country's intelligence agency, the world body told AFP on Tuesday, adding that it had no access to them for two days.

data.title: Pereira, the 'zombie city' devastated by Colombia's earthquake
data.description: PEREIRA (COLOMBIA) - Jorge Gonzalez searches with his bare hands for his aunt under the ruins of a four-story building in Pereira, one of the cities hardest hit by the powerful earthquake in Colombia that has left at least 240 dead.

data.title: Flight cancelled after child refuses to buckle seat belt
data.description: A Canadian airline was forced to cancel a cross-country flight last week after a small child would not sit down and buckle a seat belt before takeoff.

data.title: Pilot in Phuket-Delhi flight incident ‘tested positive for marijuana’
data.description: NEW DELHI - The ‌captain of an Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that suddenly lost about 300 feet of altitude last week has tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory ​drug test, multiple ⁠Indian media outlets reported on Tuesday.

data.title: Israel demolishes home of Palestinian killed in West Bank clash
data.description: TELL, Palestinian Territories - Israeli forces on Tuesday demolished the home of a Palestinian who died in July in the most lethal clash in months in the occupied West Bank, residents and the army told AFP.
